own_solution.law: The thin-lens equation gives 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, hence v = fu/(u-f) = 12(40)/(40-12) = 120/7 cm, on the opposite side of the lens from the object.
assumptions: The standard thin-lens, paraxial model applies.
The stated object distance describes the current configuration unless an added sentence subsequently changes it.
Moving the stand carrying the object moves the object with it.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TFE5A and T3FBB replace the displacement '18 cm' in their corresponding quantified renderings with 'a little', violating the stipulated preservation of the same number and unit.

notes: The individual physics problems are well-posed; the invalid verdict concerns the required matching of sentence variants. The two height statements preserve 3.5 cm: height enters the similar-triangle and magnification relations but cancels from image distance. Moving the object or its supporting stand makes u = 58 cm and v = 348/23 cm. Moving the illuminating lamp changes illumination, not the image plane. Movement during an earlier experiment does not change the explicitly stated current placement.
